title: Point the Release instructions at the one command that now does it
action:
CLAUDE.md's `## Release` section still spells out the hand-run prologue: bump the version in BOTH .claude-plugin/plugin.json AND .codex-plugin/plugin.json, run bee dev regen, make the release commit, then run scripts/release.sh to the end. As of cell roc-1 the script owns all of that -- `scripts/release.sh <VERSION>` bumps both manifests, runs bee dev regen, runs the declared test suite BEFORE anything is tagged, makes the path-scoped release commit, then tags, pushes, waits for release-binaries and verifies the assets. Leaving the checklist in place means the next agent walks it by hand and re-creates the exact drift this repo has been clearing all day.

Rewrite the `## Release` section so it teaches the one-command form: `scripts/release.sh <VERSION>` is the whole release. Mention the two flags that exist -- `--no-test` (skips the suite, warns loudly, own the risk) and `-m <subject>` (override the default `Release <VERSION>` commit subject) -- and that a re-run at an already-committed version is idempotent and just picks the release back up. Keep, because it is the rule and not a step: the release is done ONLY when the script prints its final `OK` line, and a release commit without that OK is NOT a release. Drop the now-obsolete manual bump/regen/commit instructions rather than leaving them beside the new form, so there is exactly ONE way described. Keep the section short -- it is an operating instruction, not a manual.

Do not touch any other section of CLAUDE.md and do not edit scripts/release.sh.

truths: The Release section names `scripts/release.sh <VERSION>` as the whole release
No instruction to hand-edit the two plugin manifests or to run bee dev regen by hand survives in that section
The final-OK rule is still stated
No other section of CLAUDE.md changed
